context: This prompt requires refactoring the execution modes to separate clarification (questionnaire generation) from analysis (creating analysis.md). The changes involve renaming existing files, updating references, and creating a new execution mode structure.

questions.question-text: Should the new 'clarify' mode retain all the existing behavior of the current 'analyze' mode (questionnaire generation), or should there be any modifications to how questionnaires are generated?

options.label: Retain all existing behavior exactly as-is
pros: No risk of breaking existing functionality
Simpler implementation with just file renaming
cons: Misses opportunity to improve questionnaire generation if needed

options.label: Review and potentially improve questionnaire generation logic

questions.recommendation-rationale: The prompt focuses on structural changes (renaming and creating new modes), not on improving existing functionality. Keeping behavior identical reduces risk and aligns with the prompt's intent.

questions.question-text: For the new 'analyze' mode that creates analysis.md, should the execution automatically set execution-mode back to 'no-action' after completion, similar to how clarify/plan/implement modes work?

options.label: Yes, automatically reset to no-action after completion
No, keep analyze mode active after completion
pros: Allows repeated analysis without re-enabling the mode

questions.recommendation-rationale: The execution.md file shows that all other modes (clarify, plan, implement, modification) reset to no-action after completion. Consistency is important for predictable behavior.

questions.question-text: Should the new analyze mode also execute the prompt_set_executed_on.py script after completion, similar to the implement mode?

options.label: Yes, mark prompt as executed after analyze
cons: May conflict with the intent of 'executed' flag which seems tied to implementation

options.label: No, don't mark prompt as executed
pros: Clearer separation of analysis vs implementation
Aligns with current usage where only implement mode sets executed
cons: Analysis work won't be reflected in execution tracking

questions.recommendation-rationale: The 'executed' flag appears to track implementation execution, not analysis. The analyze mode is about creating analysis documentation, not executing the prompt's implementation. This maintains clear semantics.

questions.question-text: Should there be a new flag in the work-iteration-registry.json to track whether analysis has been generated, similar to questionnaire-generated and plan-generated?

options.label: Yes, add an 'analysis-generated' boolean flag
pros: Consistent with other workflow tracking flags
Enables UI to show analysis status
Allows conditional logic based on analysis completion

options.label: No, don't add a specific flag
pros: Analysis file existence can be checked directly
cons: Less consistent with questionnaire-generated and plan-generated

questions.recommendation-rationale: Following the established pattern of questionnaire-generated and plan-generated provides consistency and better tracking. The Web UI can display this status like other flags.

questions.question-text: Should the prompt snippet key [[[ANALYZE]]] in manifest.json be updated to point to the new execution-step.analyze.md file, or should it remain pointing to analyze.md (which would no longer exist after renaming)?

options.label: Update manifest.json to point to execution-step.analyze.md
cons: Changes the snippet's purpose from standalone to execution-step

options.label: Remove the [[[ANALYZE]]] entry from manifest.json
pros: Analyze becomes a mode, not a snippet
cons: Users lose ability to insert analyze instructions via snippet key

questions.recommendation-rationale: Since analyze is becoming an execution mode (like clarify, plan, implement), it should be invoked via execution-mode setting, not via snippet insertion in prompt text. This maintains clear separation between execution modes and prompt snippets.
